result:
Understood. One decision remains before I write it up: how to build it. We covered what you want, but we never discussed the build. The three real options are below.

1. **Add it to the taproom app, in the same database.** This is the least work: one program, one database file and one backup on the Pi. The cost is that a change to the tab system could damage the batch records, and the reverse is also true. Those records must stay intact for a recall.
2. **Add it to the taproom app, but give it its own database file.** You still run one program on the same Pi, behind the same login. The batch and lot records are kept apart from the tabs, so you can back them up and keep them on their own schedule. This is a little more setup than option 1.
3. **Buy brewery software**, such as Ekos or Breww, that already does lot tracing. You build nothing, but you pay a monthly fee. You would also have to make it work with your scanner and label printer.

I recommend option 2. Recall records must outlive any change to the taproom code. A separate database file gives that protection without a second machine or a second program.

This is a project, not a quick change. I'll write the full design as a document in the repo. A reviewer will read it first, and I may come back once with a few questions. The build then starts in a fresh session from that document.

Which option do you want, or should I go with option 2?
